statement: The first line holds a text; the second holds a pattern, both lowercase. Print every 0-based index where the pattern occurs in the text, space-separated, or -1 when it occurs nowhere. Use a rolling hash: treat strings as base-B digit rows under a large modulus, compute the pattern's hash and the first window's, then slide - one subtract, one multiply, one add per step. On every hash agreement verify the window character by character before reporting it, since distinct strings can share a hash.

example.why: The pattern sits at the very start and again five characters in; the windows overlap at nothing.

hint: Precompute the highest-power term once - removing the leaving character needs it every step.
mistake: Reporting on hash equality alone; a collision then invents an occurrence that is not there.
